metaDescription: Odoo eLearning in practice: course structure, quizzes and karma, Survey certification, selling courses through eCommerce, and where SCORM and video stop.
intro: Odoo eLearning is the website_slides app. It is LGPL licensed and part of Community, not an Enterprise upsell. A course holds sections, and sections hold content items: an uploaded PDF, an image, an article written in the Odoo editor, a video by link, a quiz, or a certification. Courses run on the same partner, product, invoice and portal records as the rest of the database. That is the reason most buyers pick it over a standalone LMS. The learner, the customer and the invoice are one record.

It is not a replacement for Moodle or a corporate LMS. There is no SCORM, xAPI or AICC player. Video is played from YouTube, Google Drive or Vimeo rather than stored in Odoo. A certificate carries no expiry date. What Odoo does well is training with a commercial or operational edge: customer onboarding triggered by a confirmed sale order, partner enablement behind a portal login, and internal training whose completion record sits beside the person it belongs to.

There are two course types and they behave differently. A Training course is an ordered set of lessons with a completion percentage per attendee. A Documentation course is a browsable library with no fixed order, where a nominated group can publish content directly. The choice changes how progress reads later, so make it before the catalogue is built.
whoFor: Software, equipment and machinery vendors who want customer onboarding to start on its own once an order is confirmed.
Companies running reseller or partner enablement, where the visible course list differs by audience and has to stay behind a login.
Training businesses selling to the public, who need a catalogue, checkout, tax handling and invoices rather than a course player alone.
Employers with recurring internal training obligations who need a defensible record of who completed what, on what date, with the answer sheet behind it.
Teams already on Odoo for sales or HR, where the value is the join between a course and a customer, an order or an employee, not the player itself.
Not for institutions that must run purchased SCORM packages, need proctored exams, or want hours of video hosted in the same system. Odoo provides none of the three.

capabilities.title: Course structure and what actually uploads
capabilities.body: A course holds sections and sections hold content items. Two things upload into the database: a PDF and an image. Word, Excel and PowerPoint items come in as Google Drive links, and a video item takes a YouTube, Google Drive or Vimeo URL. Odoo reads an uploaded PDF and pre-fills the item duration from it. Any item except a certification can be flagged as a preview so visitors read it before joining, and items publish one at a time, so a live course can grow without being taken down.

capabilities.title: Quizzes, karma and what karma controls
capabilities.body: A quiz attaches to any content item, with choice based questions, a correct answer flag and a comment shown after the learner answers. Karma is awarded on the first pass and drops on later attempts: the shipped defaults are 10, 7, 5 and 2 points for the first, second, third and every further attempt, each editable per item. Karma sits on the user record, not on the attendee record. It drives ranks and badges, and the karma thresholds on a course decide who may review it, comment on a lesson or vote.

capabilities.title: Certification through Survey
capabilities.body: Certification is a Survey, joined to the course by a certification content item that requires a survey and can never be set as a preview. The survey carries the required score, which defaults to 80 percent, an attempt cap that defaults to one, an optional time limit and random question selection per section. Six certificate layouts ship, modern and classic in three colours; anything else is a report template. Each attempt is stored as a survey submission tied to the attendee, so the answer sheet survives an audit, not just the result. Survey and the certification bridge are both Community.

capabilities.title: Enrolment, visibility and the attendee record
capabilities.body: Enrolment is Open or On Invitation, with On Payment appearing once the eCommerce bridge is installed. Visibility is a separate setting with three values: Everyone, Signed In, or Course Attendees. Joining creates an attendee record holding a completion percentage and a status of invited, joined, ongoing or completed. Invitations stay valid for three months, after which an invited record with no progress is removed by the autovacuum. A course can also auto enrol the members of a user group, and one course can be set as a prerequisite for another.

capabilities.title: Selling courses
capabilities.body: Set enrolment to On Payment and the course points at a service product sold through the normal checkout, with pricelists, coupons, taxes and fiscal positions behaving as they do for any other product. Confirming the order adds the ordering partner to the course. The shop refuses a quantity above one on a course line, so a cart cannot hold five seats. Invoices, revenue and refunds stay in the accounting already in use, so finance is not reconciling a second platform against the bank.

capabilities.title: Reporting and evidence
capabilities.body: Attendee records list, group and pivot by course, status and date, and completion averages across the people on a course. The number is computed rather than stored as a fact: completion is completed items over published items, so it moves when the course moves. For anything that has to stand up later, the durable record is the survey submission with its date, score and stored answers, which no change to the course structure rewrites.

setup.title: Fix the content model before anything is uploaded
setup.body: Completion is stored per content item and is deleted with it, so restructuring a live course removes the history recorded against the items you drop. Publishing works the same way in reverse. Completion is completed items over published items, so adding one lesson to a finished course pushes every attendee below 100 percent, flips them back to ongoing and takes back the karma awarded for finishing. Decide granularity, naming, and the rule for adding content later. The usual answer is a new course version per intake rather than edits to a course people have already completed.

setup.title: Decide where the video is hosted
setup.body: A video item takes a URL and nothing else. The accepted sources are YouTube, Google Drive and Vimeo, and there is no upload path for a video file, so hosting is settled outside Odoo before the first lesson is built. Unlisted or domain restricted links keep content semi private, but check the player is reachable from the networks your learners actually sit on, including corporate proxies and countries where a given platform is blocked. PDF uploads are the part that touches infrastructure: they pass through the reverse proxy, so the nginx body size limit and the Odoo request timeout both need raising, and every file lands in the filestore and in the backup.

setup.title: Design the certification before building it
setup.body: Write the survey first: the question pool, the points per answer, the passing score, the attempt limit, the time limit and the certificate layout. The defaults are 80 percent to pass, one attempt and a ten minute limit, and each deserves a decision rather than acceptance. Then handle expiry. Odoo does not track it, so if a certificate expires you store the date on a field and drive the reminder and the re-enrolment from a scheduled action. Agree who may see failed attempts, because that answer changes the record rules on survey submissions.

setup.title: Paid enrolment, tax and payment methods
setup.body: The course product needs the correct tax, a fiscal position for learners in other countries, and a payment provider carrying the methods local buyers hold. Seats are the other decision to take here. Odoo grants the course to the partner named on the order, so a corporate sale needs its enrolment mechanism agreed before the pricing page is written, not discovered after the first invoice.

setup.title: Migrating from an existing LMS
setup.body: The files are the simple part. Learners have to be matched to existing partners by email first, or the import splits one person across two records and the history follows the wrong one. Then decide how much history to carry. Item level completions need a matching content item in Odoo, which rarely survives a restructure, so the workable compromise is one completion record per course plus the old certificate stored as an attachment on the partner.

pitfalls.title: Assuming SCORM will run
pitfalls.body: Odoo has no SCORM, xAPI or AICC player. Content bought from a library, or authored in Articulate or iSpring, will not play. Two routes work: rebuild the material as Odoo lessons with quizzes, or keep the old LMS as the player and write completion into Odoo over the API so the training record still sits with the customer or the employee. This single question moves scope more than anything else on an eLearning project, so ask it in the first meeting.

pitfalls.title: Treating karma as a grade
pitfalls.body: Karma is a gamification score. It rises with quiz passes and course completion, it is taken back when an attendee is set to uncompleted, and it is shared with the forum. It is not a mark anyone should defend to an auditor. Where someone needs a pass or fail with a date and an answer sheet, that is a certification survey, which is a different object holding different data.

pitfalls.title: Completion that nobody assessed
pitfalls.body: A learner can mark an item complete without opening it. The self mark button is withheld only on quizzes and on items that carry questions, so a course built from PDFs and videos produces completion records that prove a toggle was clicked. Where the evidence has to mean something, put questions on the items that matter and a certification at the end. Compliance reviewers ask how completion was established, and clicked is a poor answer.

pitfalls.title: Recurring compliance training
pitfalls.body: An annual refresher is not a native cycle. Retaking means setting the attendee back to uncompleted, which overwrites the current state and removes the completion karma, so the earlier proof has to exist elsewhere before the reset happens. The pattern that holds is the survey submission as the permanent record, a certification date and an expiry date stored on the employee or the attendee, and re-enrolment fired by a scheduled action.

pitfalls.title: Portal signup left on invitation only
pitfalls.body: Enrolment attaches a partner to a course, but the learner still needs a portal user to log in and read it. If the website customer account setting is left on invitation only, a buyer who has paid cannot create an account, and the access sits on a partner nobody can use. Either open free signup on the site carrying the catalogue, or send portal invitations as part of the enrolment flow. Test that path with a real external address before launch.

pitfalls.title: The course nobody can see
pitfalls.body: Four independent settings, checked in this order: the course is unpublished, individual content items are unpublished, Show Course To is set to Signed In or Course Attendees, or the enrolment policy is On Invitation when public was intended. Most reports of a broken course are one of those four, set for a different audience than the one complaining. Logs come later.

worksWith: Website, which eLearning depends on, for the public catalogue and the pages around it
eCommerce, which adds the On Payment enrolment option and the course product line
Survey, where certification, scoring, attempt limits and the certificate layout live
Gamification, installed underneath eLearning, which supplies the ranks and badges karma feeds
Forum, for per course questions that would otherwise arrive as support tickets
Email Marketing for announcements, with Marketing Automation on Enterprise for enrolment triggered follow up
Employees, where an onboarding plan activity can point a new hire at a course. No native field joins a course completion to an employee record, so that link is a small customisation
CRM, when a free course is the lead magnet and a signup should raise an opportunity against the same partner

regional.note: Course sales to individuals are simplified tax invoices under ZATCA Phase 2: 15 percent VAT, a QR code carrying the seller, the VAT number, the timestamp and the totals, and reporting to Fatoora within 24 hours of issue. Sales to a business are standard invoices needing the buyer VAT number and clearance before they are handed over. The split matters because a public catalogue and a corporate training deal run through the same product and the same checkout.

The Electronic Invoicing System covers B2B and B2G, so consumer course sales sit outside it while corporate training billed to a company does not. Large taxpayers appoint an Accredited Service Provider and go live on 1 January 2027, smaller businesses on 1 July 2027. Course products need the 5 percent VAT treatment and a fiscal position for learners abroad, since place of supply for an electronically supplied service follows the customer.

An online course sold to Indian consumers is an OIDAR supply, so GST follows the recipient location and the invoice line needs its service accounting code. Business customers above the e-invoicing turnover threshold need an IRN and a signed QR code from the portal before the invoice counts. Odoo's Indian e-invoicing module handles that once the GSP credentials are configured, but it runs on the accounting side and nothing inside eLearning triggers it.

Sales tax on training services is provincial rather than federal, so the rate and the registration follow the province, usually the Sindh Revenue Board or the Punjab Revenue Authority, while FBR digital invoicing governs the goods side. Checkout decides more than tax here. JazzCash and Easypaisa are what most buyers hold, Odoo ships a provider for neither, so a paid catalogue needs that integration answered before launch.

A course sold to a consumer is an e-Arsiv document reported to GIB, while a sale to a registered taxpayer goes out as e-Fatura over the same UBL-TR flow, both signed with a financial seal through a licensed private integrator. Odoo ships no Turkish e-invoicing connector in either edition, so that link is custom work costed separately from the eLearning build. Archived invoices have to stay retrievable inside Turkiye, which is a hosting decision rather than a setting.

Education is VAT exempt only where an eligible body supplies it, so a commercial online course is normally standard rated, and a course delivered with minimal human involvement counts as an electronically supplied service for place of supply. VAT records must be kept digitally and filed under Making Tax Digital. The HMRC submission lives in Odoo's Enterprise accounting reports, so a Community deployment holds the records in Odoo and files them through other software.

Course completion data is employee performance data, so the works council holds co-determination rights over any system recording who finished what and when. Agree the reporting scope with them before go live rather than after the first manager report circulates. Paid course invoices fall under GoBD record keeping, with the retention period for accounting vouchers now eight years, and the tax adviser will expect a DATEV export.

A provider seeking CPF or other public funding needs Qualiopi certification, and the audit asks for evidence per course: attendance or connection records, assessment results and learner feedback. Attendee records and survey submissions cover that if the evidence set is agreed before the courses are built, because a later restructure loses item level history. Paid course invoices also fall under the e-invoicing reform, phased from September 2026 for large companies and September 2027 for smaller ones.

faqs.a: No. eLearning, Survey and the certification bridge between them are Community, and so is paid enrolment through eCommerce. The Enterprise apps you might want nearby buy a different function rather than a better LMS: Marketing Automation for enrolment triggered journeys, Sign for a training agreement, Studio for adding fields without a developer, and the accounting reports that file some countries' VAT returns.

faqs.q: Do learners need paid Odoo user licences?
faqs.a: No. Attendees are portal users or public visitors, and Odoo charges per internal user. A thousand learners on portal logins add nothing to the subscription. The licences you pay for are the people building courses, reviewing submissions and reading the back office reports.

faqs.q: Can we import our existing SCORM courses?
faqs.a: There is no player for the package format, so a SCORM file will not run. Rebuilding is usually less work than it sounds where the material is text, slides and video. Where the library is large or licensed from a vendor, keep the current LMS as the player and write its completion results into Odoo over the API, so reporting and the customer or employee record still sit in one place.

faqs.q: Can we host the course videos in Odoo?
faqs.a: No. A video item takes a URL from YouTube, Google Drive or Vimeo, and the only files that upload into the database are PDFs and images. That is usually the right outcome. Video in the filestore is copied by every backup, and a video platform gives you playback quality control that Odoo does not attempt.

faqs.q: Can we sell a course to a company and enrol their whole team?
faqs.a: Not without a decision up front. Odoo grants the course to the buyer named on the order, and one course line produces one enrolment. Three routes are common: the buyer contact sends invitation links from the attendee list, your team creates portal users during onboarding, or a short extension reads the seat count from the order line and enrols the named colleagues. Invitations expire after three months, so a phased rollout needs a reminder step.

faqs.q: Does a certificate expire, and can we run annual refresher training?
faqs.a: Odoo does not track certificate expiry. The pattern that works is to store the certification date and an expiry date, keep the survey submission as the permanent proof, and use a scheduled action to notify the learner and re-enrol them. Setting an attendee back to uncompleted overwrites their progress and removes the completion karma, so capture the evidence before the reset.

faqs.q: Can one database serve courses in Arabic and English?
faqs.a: Yes for the interface and the website, including right to left layout. No for your content: a PDF, a video or an article is one file in one language. In practice you publish parallel courses per language and filter the catalogue by language or by website, which also lets pricing and the payment provider differ by market.

faqs.q: How do we show a course to some partners and hide it from others?
faqs.a: Set Show Course To to Course Attendees so only enrolled people reach the content, then control who becomes an attendee: invitation links, auto enrolment for members of a user group, or membership created by a confirmed order. The group option works on user groups rather than partner tags, so tiering by a field on the contact needs a small automation to add the right people.
